what_happened: The the person running Athena got a one-line message saying "athena go resumes from it" during the retry of job zq9x. The the person running Athena took it to mean running `athena go` on zq9x itself. They stopped a retry that was running correctly. They then ran go on the closed job, and Athena refused. They then restarted the retry. The the person running Athena never checked which job the message named. This cost one reader call and about 10 minutes. No job was judged bad.
cause: Athena does not show the the person running Athena what a command will act on, or what state the named job is in, before the the person running Athena acts. The the person running Athena works from memory of job names and from short messages. Nothing makes the the person running Athena resolve which job a message refers to, and nothing says whether stopping a running retry is safe. A hand action on a running job needs no check of its target and no confirmation. So a wrong reading is found only when a command is refused or work has already been interrupted.
prevention: Before an the person running Athena stops, closes or runs `athena go` or retry on a job, Athena prints the target's id, its state (running, closed, abandoned), and what the command will do. This includes whether it resumes a kept candidate or rebuilds. A stop on a running healthy job asks for confirmation. `athena go` on a closed job gives a clear message that names the job that is actually running or resumable. The the person running Athena default is to resolve the job id from the message and the queue before acting, and to ask when the message could name more than one job.
proposed_request: Make the commands that act on a job show their target before they act. For `athena go`, `athena retry`, `athena close` and any command that stops a running job, print the job id, its current state (running, closed, abandoned, verified), and a one-line statement of what the command will do (resume a kept candidate, rebuild, refuse). Ask for confirmation before stopping a job that is running and healthy. When `athena go` is run on a closed job, the refusal must name the job that is currently running or resumable for the same request, if one exists. Add tests: (1) stop on a running job asks for confirmation; (2) go on a closed job is refused with a message that names the running retry; (3) the output shows the state and mode for each command.
